newsitem.title: USA: House votes restrictions on family planning aid.
newsitem.headline: House votes restrictions on family planning aid.

text.p: The U.S. House of Representatives voted on Thursday to reinstate a strict ban on U.S. aid to international groups that directly or indirectly fund abortion services as part of family planning services they provide in developing countries.
The measure passed on a vote of 232-189 as an amendment to a larger State Department's authorisation bill which the House will continue debating next week.

The family planning aid restrictions would also deny all U.S. funding for the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) unless it can certify that no coercive abortions had taken place in China the previous year, or that it had ended all its activities in that country.

The primary sponsor, New Jersey Republican Chris Smith, argued the strict ban would permit U.S. funds to go only to organisations that pledge to provide only family planning help and do not provide abortions.

U.S. laws since 1973 have prohibited any federal funds from being used to pay for abortion services performed by international aid organisations. This legislation would take the law a step further and prevent the groups from using funds from other government or private sources to provide abortions.

"Money is fungible. The millions of dollars we give to a group immediately frees up other non-U.S. funds that can be used, and in this case are used, for performing and aggressively promoting abortion," Smith said in a statement.
Population Action International, a nonprofit organisation that receives no government funds, said UNFPA already does not use any U.S. funds in China.

"UNFPA has never been implicated in any incidents of coercion, and acts as a much needed link between the Chinese family planning programme and the international community," Victoria Markell, vice president of PAI said.
Planned Parenthood Federation of America president Gloria Feldt called it "nonsensical" to reduce access to family planning as a way to reduce abortions.

"Around the world there is an enormous unmet need for contraception," she said. Feldt noted that no U.S. funds are used to provide or promote abortion services and that U.S. funds are not used to promote coercive policies in China.
